title: Do So and Such: Verb-Phrase Substitution and Noun Reference
summary: Replace an identifiable action with an appropriate form of do so, distinguish action reference from states and general auxiliary do, and use such with singular, plural and uncountable nouns to refer back to an established kind. Choose the register and form that match the context.
learningObjectives: Use do so, does so, did so and doing so to refer back to an identifiable action or verb phrase with its complement.
Contrast do so with the informal alternatives do it and do that, and with the auxiliary do used in short responses.
Avoid do so as a mechanical substitute for stative predicates such as know, like or own.
Build formal reference expressions with such a/an + singular count noun, such + plural or mass noun and no such + noun.

explanation.heading: Do so replaces an understood action, not merely a verb
explanation.body: The expression do so refers to a previously mentioned activity and can stand for the main verb together with its objects or complements. It changes form according to the clause: does so, did so, doing so and done so are all possible. Its meaning must be accessible in the surrounding discourse. It can remove substantial repetition, especially when an activity is described at length.
explanation.example: The archivist scanned the letters yesterday, and her assistant will do so tomorrow.

explanation.heading: Register and nearby alternatives
explanation.body: Do so tends to sound more formal than do it or do that, which often work when an action has a specific, concrete referent. In informal speech we may use do alone after a modal or perfect auxiliary where the context makes the action obvious, especially in British English. These choices are not always interchangeable: do so describes carrying out the action, whereas do it can point to a previously mentioned task as a thing.
explanation.example: The volunteers sorted the parcels; the night team will do so after dinner.

explanation.heading: Actions versus states and short-form do
explanation.body: Do so normally replaces deliberate actions, not stative meanings such as resemble, own, believe or enjoy. Auxiliary do, by contrast, can stand for a previously mentioned predicate in a short reply or contrast even when the predicate is stative. For example, I do may repeat like the idea, but I do so is not the usual way to express liking it. Check whether do is an auxiliary substitute or the main verb in the construction.
explanation.example: Amir likes the new design, and his supervisor does too.

explanation.heading: Such refers to an established kind of noun
explanation.body: In more formal usage, such can replace a phrase equivalent to of this or that kind. Use such a or such an before a singular count noun; use such without a or an before plural or uncountable nouns. Such usually modifies an overt noun, so it is not normally a stand-alone substitute for an entire noun phrase in the constructions taught here. It can express approval, disapproval or simple classification depending on the context.
explanation.example: We have not encountered such an unusual request before.

explanation.heading: No such and distinctions from so
explanation.body: No such + noun denies the existence of the kind just described. Such behaviour, such a proposal and such arrangements point back to the type of behaviour, proposal or arrangements already identified. Do not confuse this referential such with the degree pattern so + adjective or such + (a/an) + adjective + noun. Both uses are possible, but their discourse functions differ.
explanation.example: Several people mentioned a private entrance, but the manager said there was no such entrance.

comparisons.title: An action can be replaced; a state needs a different substitute

left.label: Action: do so
left.example: The editors reviewed the files, and the interns did so later.
left.note: Did so replaces the identifiable act of reviewing the files.

right.label: State: auxiliary do
right.example: Nina knows the answer, and Farid does too.
right.note: Does substitutes for knows the answer; does so is not the neutral choice for this stative meaning.

comparisons.title: Countability determines the form after such

left.label: Singular count: such a/an
left.example: The committee rejected such a proposal.
left.note: Proposal is singular and countable, so a is required.

right.label: Plural or uncountable: such
right.example: Such delays are costly, and such confusion is avoidable.
right.note: Delays is plural and confusion is uncountable, so no article follows such.

examples.sentence: The organisers checked every registration and asked the venue staff to do so as well.
examples.note: Do so replaces check every registration.

examples.sentence: The technician had promised to calibrate the sensor and had already done so by noon.
examples.note: Done so can follow a perfect auxiliary and refer back to a completed activity.

examples.sentence: I promised to help with the move, and I probably will do.
examples.note: Informal British usage may place do after a modal as a shorter action substitute.

examples.sentence: The children enjoy the exhibition, and their grandparents do too.
examples.note: Auxiliary do repeats a stative attitude; do so would be unnatural in the intended sense.

examples.sentence: We cannot approve such changes without consulting residents.
examples.note: Such changes points back to a kind of change already in the discussion.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The researchers copied the data, and their assistants do so yesterday.
commonMistakes.correct: The researchers copied the data, and their assistants did so yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: A past-time action requires did so, not present-tense do so.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Mara admires the architect, and her brother does so too.
commonMistakes.correct: Mara admires the architect, and her brother does too.
commonMistakes.why: Admire is a stative meaning here; auxiliary does is the natural predicate substitute.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The committee has never received such an requests before.
commonMistakes.correct: The committee has never received such requests before.
commonMistakes.why: Plural requests takes such without an article.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Some witnesses described a secret tunnel, but there was no such a tunnel.
commonMistakes.correct: Some witnesses described a secret tunnel, but there was no such tunnel.
commonMistakes.why: No such + singular noun does not take a or an.

studyTips: After each instance of do so, replace it mentally with the earlier complete action and check whether its tense and participants still make sense.
Write contrasting pairs using a dynamic verb such as inspect and a state verb such as know; use did so for the action and did or does for the state.
Sort your own examples of such into singular count, plural and uncountable categories, then test whether a/an, no or another determiner is permitted.

exercises.prompt: The team inspected the lifts on Monday, and the contractor ___ on Tuesday. Choose the formal substitute.
choices: did so
did such
does so
exercises.feedback: Did so replaces inspected the lifts and agrees with the past time on Tuesday.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence naturally substitutes for a repeated state rather than an action?
choices: Zoe owns a telescope, and Karl does so too.
Zoe owns a telescope, and Karl does too.
Zoe owns a telescope, and Karl is doing so too.
exercises.feedback: Does too uses auxiliary do to repeat the stative predicate owns a telescope.

exercises.prompt: The authorities warned against ___ delays. The referent is plural and already described.
choices: such a
so
such
exercises.feedback: Such directly modifies the plural noun delays; such a is restricted to singular count nouns.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct formal denial of an alleged secret agreement.
choices: There is no such an agreement.
There is no such agreement.
There is not so agreement.
exercises.feedback: No such + singular count noun is grammatical without an additional article.

exercises.prompt: The panel reviewed the evidence, and the second panel ___ ___ the following day. Use the past form of do so.
acceptedAnswers: did so
exercises.feedback: Did so avoids repeating reviewed the evidence.

exercises.prompt: The curator offered to restore the frame and has already ___ ___. Complete the formal perfect construction.
acceptedAnswers: done so
exercises.feedback: Has done so stands for has restored the frame.

exercises.prompt: Complete with exactly two words: We have rarely seen ___ ___ complicated case. Use such + article.
acceptedAnswers: such a
exercises.feedback: Such a comes before the singular count noun case modified by complicated.

exercises.prompt: The archive has no ___ records of the kind described in the letter. Supply one word.
acceptedAnswers: such
exercises.feedback: No such records denies records of the previously mentioned type.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The lawyers filed the application, and the clerks does so later.
acceptedAnswers: The lawyers filed the application, and the clerks did so later.
exercises.feedback: The previously described action happened in the past, so did so matches the intended time.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Iris believes the claim, and Leo does so too.
acceptedAnswers: Iris believes the claim, and Leo does too.
exercises.feedback: Use auxiliary does, not does so, to substitute for the state of believing the claim.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The report contains such an evidence that the decision was reconsidered.
acceptedAnswers: The report contains such evidence that the decision was reconsidered.
exercises.feedback: Evidence is uncountable and cannot take an; such evidence is the correct form.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We expected a handwritten note, but there was no such a note.
acceptedAnswers: We expected a handwritten note, but there was no such note.
exercises.feedback: Remove the article after no such in this reference construction.

speakingExercises.prompt: Retell without repeating the action. Facts: The guard locked the side gate. The caretaker did the same afterwards. Begin with "The guard" and use did so.
acceptedAnswers: The guard locked the side gate. The caretaker did so afterwards.
speakingExercises.feedback: Did so replaces locked the side gate and keeps the earlier past time.

speakingExercises.prompt: Express a formal intention to repeat an action. Facts: The team will update the records; the manager will also update them. Begin with "The team" and use will do so.
acceptedAnswers: The team will update the records. The manager will do so too.
speakingExercises.feedback: Will do so refers back to the planned act of updating the records.

speakingExercises.prompt: Express the past completed substitute. Facts: Mina promised to notify the clients and has already notified them. Start with "Mina" and use has already done so.
acceptedAnswers: Mina promised to notify the clients and has already done so.
speakingExercises.feedback: Done so can stand for notifying the clients after has.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the stative substitute aloud: "Ali understands the rule, and Bea does so too."
acceptedAnswers: Ali understands the rule, and Bea does too.
speakingExercises.feedback: Does too substitutes for understands the rule without treating a state as an action.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use such a to refer to a previously discussed singular proposal. Facts: We / cannot / approve / such a / risky proposal. Give one sentence.
acceptedAnswers: We cannot approve such a risky proposal.
We can't approve such a risky proposal.
speakingExercises.feedback: Such a precedes a singular count noun with an adjective.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use such with a plural count noun. Facts: Such / misunderstandings / are / avoidable. Say the complete sentence.
acceptedAnswers: Such misunderstandings are avoidable.
speakingExercises.feedback: Plural misunderstandings has no indefinite article after such.

speakingExercises.prompt: Deny the existence of the alleged rule. Facts: There / is / no such / rule. Say one complete sentence.
acceptedAnswers: There is no such rule.
There's no such rule.
speakingExercises.feedback: No such rule denies that a rule of the mentioned type exists.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give two sentences in this exact order. Action: The staff cleaned the gallery yesterday; the volunteers did the same today. State: Rosa likes the gallery; Malik shares the opinion. Use did so and does too.
acceptedAnswers: The staff cleaned the gallery yesterday, and the volunteers did so today. Rosa likes the gallery, and Malik does too.
speakingExercises.feedback: Did so substitutes for cleaning, while does too substitutes for a state of liking.

listeningExercises.audioText: The engineers will inventory the equipment this afternoon, and the assistants will do so tomorrow.
listeningExercises.prompt: What activity will the assistants also carry out?
choices: They will inventory the equipment.
They will replace the equipment.
They will deliver the equipment.
listeningExercises.feedback: Do so refers back to the previously mentioned act of inventorying the equipment.

listeningExercises.audioText: Leila prefers the quiet room, and her colleague does too.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is the function of does in the second clause?
choices: It describes a second physical action.
It repeats a statement about a preference.
It means that someone is carrying out a formal duty.
listeningExercises.feedback: Does too replaces prefers the quiet room, which describes a preference rather than an activity.

listeningExercises.audioText: The auditor examined the contract yesterday. Her assistant did so this morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: Transcribe the exact two-word expression meaning performed that action.
acceptedAnswers: did so
listeningExercises.feedback: Did so refers to the act of examining the contract.

listeningExercises.audioText: A six-hour journey without a break? Such a timetable would be unreasonable for most passengers.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the speaker say about the proposed timetable?
choices: They consider that type of timetable unreasonable.
They say every timetable is unacceptable.
They say that the timetable has already been approved.
listeningExercises.feedback: Such a timetable means a timetable of the type just described; the speaker rejects it as unreasonable.

listeningExercises.audioText: Someone told me visitors had to sign three forms, but there is no such rule at this museum.
choices: The need to inspect the room.
The existence of the kind of rule described.
The date when the rule was announced.
listeningExercises.feedback: No such rule denies the existence of a rule of that kind.

listeningExercises.audioText: The caretaker promised to check every lock, and she has already done so.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which statement best reflects what happened?
choices: The assistant has not completed the promised checks.
The assistant is considering the checks.
The assistant has already completed the promised checks.
listeningExercises.feedback: Has already done so refers to the completed act of checking the locks.

listeningExercises.audioText: There were rumours of a new warehouse, but the director said there were no such plans.
listeningExercises.prompt: Transcribe the exact two-word phrase following no in the statement.
acceptedAnswers: such plans
listeningExercises.feedback: No such plans denies the existence of plans of that kind.

listeningExercises.audioText: Several guests left the hall without permission. The organiser said such careless behaviour was unacceptable.
listeningExercises.prompt: Transcribe the exact two-word reference phrase before behaviour.
acceptedAnswers: such careless
listeningExercises.feedback: Such careless behaviour means behaviour of the kind just described.
